**Finding: compliant (no redline proposed).**

TrueLink has no audit right to constrain:

- **§ 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client)** — the natural home for an inspection/records right — contains none; its only access provision (§ 8(c) "Limitation on Access") restricts *Client's* internal access to the Interface.
- **§ 5–6 (Compensation; Documentation and Disputes)** runs in our favour: Client is entitled to documentation supporting amounts charged and may contest charges. There is no reciprocal TrueLink right to verify Client usage or fees.
- **§ 3(e)** gives Client real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files, so usage data verification sits with us, not with TrueLink.
- No provision anywhere grants TrueLink access to Client systems, premises or records for verification. The only access obligation on Client (§ 9, Y2K remediation) is Client-requested repair access at TrueLink's sole cost.

Because there is no audit right binding Client, there is no frequency, notice, location or cost-allocation exposure — a position better than both the preferred (once/12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, off-site, Vendor cost unless >5% underpayment, no system access) and fallback checklists. Inserting audit parameters would create a Vendor right that does not presently exist, so we leave the clause set untouched.
